瓦格納低音號主要採用黃銅製造，包括管身、導管、活塞及喇叭口均為黃銅合金構成。活塞: The Wagner tuba is made mainly of brass: the body, the tubing, the valves and the bell are all of brass alloy. The valve system is of rotary design, its internal parts cast in fine brass. Inside, a special brass alloy is used to improve the resonance. The mouthpiece is of silver or silver-plated brass, which makes the tone brighter. On some better instruments the valve springs are of stainless steel, for durability and steady mechanical action.
瓦格納低音號擁有獨特而深沉的音色，介於法國號的溫潤與低音號的厚重之間。其音質帶有: The Wagner tuba has a distinctive, deep timbre that lies between the warmth of the horn and the weight of the tuba. Its tone has a mysterious darkness while keeping a metallic sheen, and it is often described as "smoky" and "otherworldly". Its resonance has both the round echo of the horn and the sweep of brass, with a wide range and a steady tone. The bass is full and strong, the middle warm and beautiful, and the treble shows a bright carrying power. Compared with the trombone its tone is gentler and finer; compared with the horn it has more of a deep solemnity. These qualities make it the ideal choice for grand narrative and dramatic tension.
瓦格納低音號是標準管弦樂團裡不常用的氣鳴銅管樂器，起源歐洲並在全球使用。它用於瓦: The Wagner tuba is an aerophone brass instrument not much used in the standard orchestra; it originated in Europe and is used worldwide. It is used in Wagner's four-opera cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen, played by horn players as a second instrument, to bridge the tone of horn and trombone; Bruckner's Seventh Symphony and his Eighth and Ninth use four of them; Richard Strauss's Alpine Symphony also calls for it. It also appears in works by composers such as Bartók.
瓦格納低音號由瓦格納為《尼伯龍根的指環》委託製作，用以銜接圓號與長號。他原想用長: Wagner commissioned the Wagner tuba for Der Ring des Nibelungen, to bridge the tone of horn and trombone. He first wanted to use the trombone for the Nordic legendary subjects, and then turned to a new instrument, the "Tuben", taking the conical bore and mouthpiece of the horn rather than the cylindrical bore of the saxhorn. In 1853 he visited Sax, and the instrument was finally made by C. W. Moritz of Berlin. There is also a version designed to be played by trombonists. From the 20th century makers have combined F and B flat into a double instrument. Bruckner, Richard Strauss and other composers later took it up.

The Wagner tuba is an aerophone brass instrument, Hornbostel–Sachs number 423.231-12, not much used in the orchestra. It was commissioned by Richard Wagner for the opera cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen, to bridge the tone of horn and trombone. It has four rotary valves worked by the left hand, the same mouthpiece and fingering as the horn, and it is usually played by horn players as a second instrument; its bore lies between the euphonium's and the horn's, and it comes as a tenor in B flat and a bass in F.
